rules.title: Review rules
rules.intro: This platform runs on what participants actually experienced. A few simple rules keep the reviews useful.

honest.title: Be honest
honest.body: Write only about hackathons you took part in yourself. Do not pass on what you heard from others as fact.

specific.title: Be specific
specific.body: A review that says “it was bad” helps no one. Say what happened: how many hours the schedule slipped, how many days the reply took, when the prize arrived.

noInsults.title: No insults
noInsults.body: Criticize the organizers all you want. Personal insults, threats and harassment are not allowed.

noFabrication.title: Do not make things up
noFabrication.body: False information, advertising and coordinated reviews against competitors are removed.

anonymity.title: How anonymity works
anonymity.body: In an anonymous review your name is not shown on the site. But a moderator can see who wrote it, in order to prevent abuse. That access is not there to protect anonymity — it is there to stop rule-breaking.

moderation.title: Moderation
moderation.body: Reviews that break the rules are hidden and excluded from the rating. One review per hackathon per user. You can edit your review at any time.

legal.title: Legal note
legal.body: Reviews on this site are the personal opinions of their authors, not a verdict from the platform. Scores follow a structured set of criteria. If you see an error or a violation, use the report button.

about.title: Why this platform exists
about.lead: Uzbekistan runs more hackathons every year. The quality varies wildly. This platform makes that difference visible.

problem.title: The problem
problem.body: The organizer says “finalists will be announced very soon” and then goes quiet. Judging criteria are vague. Prizes are promised, then delivered months late. All of it stays inside closed Telegram chats, and the next participant walks in knowing none of it.

solution.title: The fix
solution.body: An open, structured rating. Every hackathon is scored in five clear categories: organization, communication, judging, prizes and venue. Only people who took part can score. The organizer's overall record across all of their hackathons is visible too.

one.title: Reading is always open
one.body: Reading reviews will never require an account.

two.title: No fake reviews
two.body: The platform never writes reviews itself and never posts made-up scores.

three.title: Organizers get a right of reply
three.body: An organizer can post an official response, and it appears under the review.

about.contactBody: Suggestions, bugs, partnerships — write to us on Telegram.
